reviewed_note: SU.FOL.OM3: ages 45-80 within 12 months of an acute coronary or cerebral ischaemic event. The served HR 1.08 (0.79-1.47) is the omega-3 factorial contrast on major vascular events, 81 vs 76, printed in the OA full text. ITT stated. The ISRCTN41926726 parent is held.

population.span: Men and women aged 45–80 years who had had an acute coronary or cerebral ischaemic event within the 12 months before randomisation were eligible to participate.

endpoint.span: The primary end point was the first major cardiovascular event—non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, or death from cardiovascular disease

estimate.span: Allocation to omega 3 fatty acids was not associated with any significant effect on major vascular events (81 v 76 patients, hazard ratio 1.08 (0.79 to 1.47), P=0.64; fig 4).

ci.span: Allocation to omega 3 fatty acids was not associated with any significant effect on major vascular events (81 v 76 patients, hazard ratio 1.08 (0.79 to 1.47), P=0.64; fig 4).

analysis_set.span: All analyses were conducted according to the principle of intention to treat.

treatment_strategy.span: Daily dietary supplement containing 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (560 μg), vitamin B-6 (3 mg), and vitamin B-12 (20 μg) or placebo; and containing omega 3 fatty acids (600 mg of eicosapentanoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid at a ratio of 2:1) or placebo.

follow_up.span: The median follow-up time was 4.7 years (mean 4.2 (SD 1.0) years) with a total of 10 656 person years. All participants completed their scheduled treatment by 1 July 2009.

entry_population_reading.span: Men and women aged 45–80 years who had had an acute coronary or cerebral ischaemic event within the 12 months before randomisation were eligible to participate.

entry_population.extractor_why: Adults with recent coronary or cerebral ischaemic events fall within the question's cardiovascular-risk population; analyses were intention to treat.
